Strategy: Stripper Level (xmeas_15) is a liquid accumulation state whose genuine physical drivers are (a) upstream liquid mass entering the process train (approximated here by A Feed Flow, xmeas_1, since the direct inflow variable, Separator Underflow xmeas_14, is a forbidden cross-unit accumulation-state neighbor and was excluded per the trap rule) and (b) the Stripper Underflow Valve position (xmv_8), which sets the liquid outflow rate from the stripper bottom (negative/outflow term). I added Stripper Steam Flow (xmeas_19) as a secondary negative term: steam entering the column vaporizes/strips light components which exit overhead to the condenser rather than remaining as bottoms liquid, so higher steam flow at fixed underflow valve position tends to reduce the net liquid accumulation rate — a legitimate mass-balance-adjacent mechanism (vapor-liquid mass transfer removing liquid-phase mass), not merely a correlated controller response, since xmeas_19 is itself a manipulated-flow-adjacent measurement rather than a target-unit state variable.

All three inputs are flow/valve-position variables that cross the stripper's mass boundary, consistent with law #1 (mass balance): xmeas_1 is treated as an inflow proxy (+), xmv_8 is the direct bottoms outflow actuator (- in formula, + expected coefficient), and xmeas_19 is treated as an indirect vapor-side outflow driver (- in formula, + expected coefficient). If the sign check fails for xmeas_1 (plausible, since it is two units upstream and heavily buffered by the reactor/separator before reaching the stripper), I will drop it and rely on xmv_8 and xmeas_19 alone, or reconsider law #4 (valve/orifice nonlinearity) for the xmv_8 term in the next iteration.
